sources.title: NYC Open Streets 2026
sources.publisher: New York City Department of Transportation
sources.usage: Precedent for streets that switch between full closure, limited local access and ordinary operation on explicitly published days and hours while maintaining emergency/access requirements.
sources.limitations: Governance, liability, street geometry and legal authority differ from Beijing; used only as a transferable operating mechanism, not as a local standard.

sources.title: Code the Curb
sources.usage: Precedent for machine-readable public-right-of-way inventories and communicating static/dynamic curb regulations to people and mobility services.
sources.limitations: LADOT policy and curb inventory are jurisdiction-specific; concept transfer is limited to digital regulation representation and auditability.

sources.title: Curb Data Specification (CDS) 1.0
sources.usage: Precedent for publishing curb locations/regulations, events and metrics through an interoperable data structure; informs the TimeSlot Contract's machine-readable philosophy.
sources.limitations: CDS is a curb-management data specification, not a Beijing planning or AV safety standard.

sources.title: Autonomous Vehicles — Safety & Testing
sources.usage: Precedent for separating controlled AV safety assessment/testing from public-road deployment, requiring operational safeguards and data recording.
sources.limitations: Singapore law and CETRAN requirements do not apply in Beijing; this source supports the design principle that testing is not permission and that fail-safe/human accountability must be explicit.

sources.title: School Streets
sources.usage: Precedent for temporary motor-traffic restrictions tied to school drop-off and pick-up times, demonstrating predictable time-based street rights.
sources.limitations: Local traffic orders and enforcement differ; used only to illustrate time-defined public-space operation.

sources.title: Rues aux écoles
sources.usage: Precedent for converting street space around schools into safer pedestrian/public space, supporting the youth-friendly and reversible-public-realm dimension.
sources.limitations: Not all Paris school streets use the same timing/closure mechanism; transfer is conceptual rather than regulatory.
